Asset.name: ABB IRC5 Robot Controller
Asset.description: IRC5 based robot system controller covered by the trouble shooting manual.

Component.name: Main fuse Q1
Component.description: Mains fuse inside the Drive Module.

Component.name: Circuit breaker F6
Component.description: Circuit breaker F6 in the controller mains circuit.

Component.name: Mains power supply
Component.description: Mains power supply to the robot system.

Component.name: Circuit breaker F5
Component.description: Circuit breaker for the Control Module service outlet.

Component.name: Earth fault protection F4
Component.description: Earth fault protection for the service outlet.

Component.description: Joystick on the FlexPendant used to jog the robot.

Component.description: Robot axis gearbox with oil filling.

Component.description: Bearings in motors, gearboxes and joints.

Symptom.name: Controller not responding
Symptom.description: Robot controller not responding; LED indicators not lit.

Symptom.name: All LEDs are OFF at Controller
Symptom.description: No LEDs at all are lit on the Control Module or the Drive Module.

Symptom.name: No voltage in service outlet
Symptom.description: No voltage is available in the Control Module service outlet.

Symptom.name: Problem jogging the robot
Symptom.description: The system can be started but the joystick on the FlexPendant does not work.

Symptom.name: Oil and grease stains on motors and gearboxes
Symptom.description: The area surrounding the motor or gearbox shows signs of oil leaks.

Symptom.name: Mechanical noise
Symptom.description: A faulty bearing emits scraping, grinding, or clicking noises shortly before failing.

Symptom.name: Manipulator crashes on power down
Symptom.description: When Motors OFF is active the manipulator collapses under its own weight.

Symptom.name: Problem releasing Robot brakes
Symptom.description: The internal robot brakes do not release, no robot movement is possible.

FailureMode.name: Main fuse (Q1) might have tripped
FailureMode.description: The mains fuse Q1 inside the Drive Module has tripped.

FailureMode.name: Circuit breaker F6 is malfunctioning or open
FailureMode.description: Circuit breaker F6 (if used) is malfunctioning or open for any other reason.

FailureMode.name: The system is not supplied with power
FailureMode.description: The system is not supplied with power.

FailureMode.name: Tripped circuit breaker (F5)
FailureMode.description: The circuit breaker F5 has tripped.

FailureMode.name: Tripped earth fault protection (F4)
FailureMode.description: The earth fault protection F4 has tripped.

FailureMode.name: The joystick is malfunctioning
FailureMode.description: The joystick on the FlexPendant is malfunctioning.

FailureMode.name: Leaking seal between gearbox and motor
FailureMode.description: The seal between gearbox and motor is leaking oil.

FailureMode.name: Gearbox overfilled with oil
FailureMode.description: The gearbox is overfilled with oil.

FailureMode.name: Faulty power supply to the brake
FailureMode.description: The power supply to the motor holding brake is faulty.

FailureMode.name: Brake contactor (K44) does not work correctly
FailureMode.description: The brake contactor K44 does not work correctly.

FailureMode.name: Supply voltage 24V BRAKE missing
FailureMode.description: The 24V BRAKE supply voltage is missing.

FailureMode.name: Drive Module power supply failure
FailureMode.description: The Drive Module power supply receives 230 VAC but its LEDs remain off.

FailureMode.name: Faulty motor holding brake
FailureMode.description: The holding brake integral to a motor is faulty.

FailureMode.name: Faulty brake on the robot axis

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace the Drive Module power supply
CorrectiveAction.description: Replace the Drive Module power supply when incoming voltage is correct but its LEDs remain off.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: If the power supply incoming voltage is correct (230 VAC) but the LEDs still do not work, replace the Drive Module power supply.
CorrectiveAction.source_title: ABB IRC5 Robot Controller Trouble Shooting Manual

CorrectiveAction.name: Switch on the main switch and supply the system with power
CorrectiveAction.description: Switch on the main switch and restore system power.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Restore the system power supply after switching on the main switch.
CorrectiveAction.source_title: ABB IRC5 Robot Controller Trouble Shooting Manual

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace the motor as a complete unit
CorrectiveAction.description: Replace a faulty motor and its integral holding brake as a complete unit.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Replace the motor as a complete unit if it is found faulty.
CorrectiveAction.source_title: ABB IRC5 Robot Controller Trouble Shooting Manual

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace the faulty brake
CorrectiveAction.description: Replace the single faulty robot-axis brake.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Replace the faulty brake if just one of the brakes malfunctions.
CorrectiveAction.source_title: ABB IRC5 Robot Controller Trouble Shooting Manual

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace seals and gaskets as specified
CorrectiveAction.description: Replace leaking seals and gaskets as specified for the robot.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Inspect all seals and gaskets between motor and gearbox. Replace seals and gaskets as specified in the product manual for the robot.
CorrectiveAction.source_title: ABB IRC5 Robot Controller Trouble Shooting Manual

CorrectiveAction.name: Make sure the bearing has sufficient lubrication
CorrectiveAction.description: Make sure the bearing has sufficient lubrication.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: Restore sufficient bearing lubrication as specified in the product manual for the robot.
CorrectiveAction.source_title: ABB IRC5 Robot Controller Trouble Shooting Manual

evidence.quote: Cause: main fuse (Q1) might have tripped.
If the power supply incoming voltage is correct (230 VAC) but the LEDs still do not work
circuit breaker F6 (if used) is malfunctioning or open for any other reason
the system is not supplied with power
Make sure the system is supplied with power. Use a voltmeter to measure incoming mains voltage.
tripped circuit breaker (F5)
replace the Drive Module power supply
tripped earth fault protection (F4)
Possible causes. The symptom can be caused by (the causes are listed in order of probability): faulty brake; faulty power supply to the brake.
the joystick is malfunctioning
leaking seal between gearbox and motor
Inspect all seals and gaskets between motor and gearbox. The different manipulator models use different types of seals. Replace seals and gaskets as specified in the product manual for the robot.
gearbox overfilled with oil
If found faulty, the motor must be replaced as a complete unit as detailed in the product manual for the robot.
loss of lubrication in bearings
Make sure the bearing has sufficient lubrication.
faulty power supply to the brake
faulty brake on the robot axis
brake contactor (K44) does not work correctly
If just one of the brakes malfunctions, the brake at hand is probably faulty and must be replaced.
supply voltage 24V BRAKE missing
